name: form
title: Form
description: Forms on react-hook-form with a Standard Schema (Zod, Valibot, Effect): FormField binds one registry control by name, pending submit, server errors mapped to fields, a live root error, focus on the first invalid field, and messages in any language or i18n library.
docs: `<Form schema defaultValues onSubmit messages label>` with `<FormField name label description required>` around one control: Input, Textarea, NumberInput, Select, Combobox, Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroup, Slider, DatePicker, SegmentedControl or ToggleGroup bind by `name` (no `control` or `render`); `bind` or `render` for anything else, `useFormField()` inside a custom control. Give every field a default value. `onSubmit(values, { setError })` may return a Promise: the submit Button shows `loading`, fields are disabled (`disableWhilePending={false}` keeps them), a second submit is ignored. Throw a `FormServerError(message, fieldErrors)`, `{ fieldErrors, message }` or a Standard Schema issue list (`toFormErrors`) to put errors on fields and in `<FormRootError />` (an `Alert tone="destructive" live`); any other error shows its message there. Focus then goes to the first invalid field, or to the root error. Messages: `messages={formMessagesEs}`, a dictionary, or a function of the issue for i18next, FormatJS or Lingui (`createFormMessages(t)` makes one from `t(key, params)`, keys `form.<code>`); `FormField messages` wins over the form's. An issue is `{ code, field, label, params, message }`; codes: `required`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `minItems`, `maxItems`, `min`, `max` (params `min`/`max`), `email`, `url`, `pattern`, `invalid`, `server`, or a schema message that looks like a key (`form.email.taken`), or a server error's own `code`. Agents fill fields through their own parts and call the form's `submit` and `reset` when it has a `label`; `<FormActions tone="destructive" confirm="…">` puts `data-agent-confirm` on the submit button and hides the form's `submit` from agents.
